demo_input.text: The cat sat on the mat because it was tired.

step_explanations.title: Validate Input and Highlight Word
step_explanations.description: Check text is valid and the highlight word exists in the text.

input_preview.text: The cat sat on the mat because it was tired.

step_explanations.why_it_matters: Attention needs valid tokens to compute meaningful query-key-value interactions.

step_explanations.title: Generate Q, K, V Vectors
step_explanations.description: Apply learned linear projections to input embeddings to create Query, Key, and Value vectors for each token.
step_explanations.formula: Q = XW^Q, K = XW^K, V = XW^V
step_explanations.why_it_matters: Q, K, V allow the model to compute different types of relationships (Q=what to look for, K=what to match against, V=what info to retrieve).

step_explanations.title: Compute Attention Scores (QK^T)
step_explanations.description: Calculate dot products between Query of each token and Keys of all tokens to measure similarity.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: High QK^T scores mean strong relationship - the query token finds relevant info in the key token.

step_explanations.title: Apply Softmax to Get Attention Weights
step_explanations.description: Apply softmax to attention scores so weights sum to 1, making them interpretable as percentages.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: These weights show exactly which words the model focuses on when processing each word.

step_explanations.title: Weight Values to Get Output
step_explanations.description: Multiply attention weights by Value vectors to produce the final output representation for each token.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: The weighted sum creates a context-aware representation that incorporates relevant info from all tokens.

formula_cards.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
formula_cards.explanation: Compute similarity between queries and keys (QK^T), scale by √d_k, apply softmax to get weights, then weight the values V.
formula_cards.example: For 'it', Q·K^T gives similarity to all words; softmax gives weights like [0.3, 0.45, 0.15, ...]

formula_cards.title: Multi-Head Attention
formula_cards.formula: MultiHead(Q,K,V) = Concat(head₁, ..., head_h)W^O, where head_i = Attention(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)
formula_cards.explanation: Run attention h times in parallel with different learned projections, then concatenate and project.
formula_cards.example: With 8 heads, the model can attend to 8 different relationship types simultaneously (syntax, semantics, coreference, etc.)

formula_cards.title: Attention Weight Interpretation
formula_cards.explanation: The attention weight α_{ij} represents how much token i attends to token j. Higher weight = stronger relationship.

variables.α_{ij}: attention weight from token i to token j

formula_cards.example: α_{it,cat} = 0.45 means 'it' attends to 'cat' with weight 0.45 (the strongest connection)

hover_annotations.definition: Vector representing what a token is looking for in other tokens.
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: Q_i = X_i·W^Q - transformed input that expresses the 'query'
hover_annotations.example: For 'it', Q might look for nouns that could be the referent (cat, mat, ...)
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Thinking Q, K, V are the same as input embeddings (they're learned transformations)

hover_annotations.definition: A number between 0 and 1 showing how much token i focuses on token j. Row sums to 1.
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: α_{ij} = softmax(Q_i·K_j/√d_k) - high score means strong attention
hover_annotations.example: α_{it,cat} = 0.45 → 'it' attends to 'cat' with 45% of its attention
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Thinking high attention always means correct interpretation (it's a statistical pattern, not true understanding)

references.title: Attention Is All You Need
references.relevance: Original Transformer paper introducing Scaled Dot-Product Attention and Multi-Head Attention.

references.title: The Illustrated Transformer
references.relevance: Excellent visual explanation of attention mechanisms with intuitive diagrams.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: Attention is like highlighting text. When the model reads 'it', it highlights 'cat' because that's what 'it' refers to.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Use a sentence with clear coreference. Show the attention heatmap with colors.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V. Q, K, V are learned projections. Multi-head runs h attention mechanisms in parallel.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Scaling by √d_k prevents dot products from getting too large (which would push softmax into regions with tiny gradients).

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: Attention enables global dependency modeling (any token can attend to any other, regardless of distance). Research shows attention patterns: some heads do syntax, some do coreference, some do position. Limitations: O(n²) complexity in sequence length.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Limitations: quadratic complexity O(n²·d) in sequence length n. Efficient variants: Sparse Attention, Linformer, Reformer. Interpretability: attention weights are post-hoc explanations, not always faithful (Jain & Wallace, 2019).

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: Attention is O(n²·d) where n=sequence length, d=model dimension. Use torch.nn.MultiheadAttention. Temperature=1.0 is standard; lower = sharper weights.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Complexity: O(n²·d) self-attention. Memory: O(n²) for attention matrix. API: torch.nn.MultiheadAttention, tf.keras.layers.MultiHeadAttention.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: Attention is the core innovation of Transformers. Show how it solves the sequential bottleneck of RNNs.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Quiz: What do Q, K, V represent? Exercise: Compute attention manually for a 3-word sentence. Discuss: Why scale by √d_k?

research_context: The Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) replaced recurrence with attention, enabling parallelization and better long-range dependency modeling. Attention mechanisms have become the foundation of modern NLP, with applications beyond NLP (vision, multimodal).

teaching_notes.summary: Scaled Dot-Product Attention allows tokens to attend to all other tokens, creating context-aware representations.
quiz_questions: What do Q, K, and V represent in attention?
Why do we scale by √d_k in the attention formula?
Compute attention weights manually for a 3-token sentence with d_k=2.
classroom_demo_tips: Visualize attention as a heatmap with token labels
Show how attention changes for different heads
Compare attention patterns for syntax vs. coreference
common_misconceptions: Attention weights always show true model reasoning (false - they're correlational, not causal)
More heads always better (false - diminishing returns, more compute)
